instructions.content: Apply Bases for dynamic views of vault notes by tag/folder/property (task trackers, reading lists, dashboards); do not apply it for one-off note organisation, static Markdown tables, or content that does not come from frontmatter properties.
instructions.original_snippets: When to apply: Creating dynamic views of vault notes by tag, folder, or property ... When NOT to apply: One-off note organisation, static Markdown tables, or displaying content that does not come from frontmatter properties.

instructions.content: Build a base by creating the file, defining scope with filters, optionally adding formulas, configuring one or more views, then validating the YAML and testing it in Obsidian.
instructions.original_snippets: 1. Create the file ... 2. Define scope ... 3. Add formulas (optional) ... 4. Configure views ... 5. Validate ... 6. Test in Obsidian

instructions.content: Filters can be applied globally (top-level filters key, affecting every view) or per-view (a filters key inside one view entry).
instructions.original_snippets: Global filters apply to ALL views in the base ... View-specific filters

instructions.content: There are three kinds of properties: note properties (from frontmatter), file properties (file.* metadata), and formula properties (computed, referenced as formula.<name>).
instructions.original_snippets: Three Types of Properties: 1. Note properties ... 2. File properties ... 3. Formula properties - Computed values: formula.my_formula

instructions.content: NEVER use file.name for a display column when file.basename is available; file.name includes the .md extension and clutters the output.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER use file.name as a display column in table or cards views when you want clean note titles ... file.basename returns only the title without the extension

instructions.content: NEVER call .round(), .floor(), or .ceil() directly on the result of a date subtraction; that result is a Duration, not a Number, so those methods are undefined on it. Access a numeric field like .days first.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER call .round(), .floor(), or .ceil() directly on the result of a date subtraction ... Access .days, .hours, .minutes, etc. before applying any Number methods.

instructions.content: NEVER call a property-dependent function such as date(due_date) without first guarding for the property being missing; wrap it in if(property, ..., fallback) or the entire formula column blanks out for every row.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER call property-dependent functions such as date(due_date) without first checking that the property exists ... Always wrap property-dependent expressions in if(property, ..., fallback).

instructions.content: NEVER reference formula.X in order or properties without a matching key X under the top-level formulas block; Obsidian silently drops the column with no error.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER reference formula.X in order or properties without a matching key in the formulas block ... Obsidian silently drops the column.

instructions.content: NEVER leave a YAML string value unquoted when it contains a structural character such as : { } [ ] , & * # ? | - < > = ! % @ or a backtick; quote it or the whole base fails to load.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER leave strings unquoted when they contain characters that YAML treats as structural syntax ... An unquoted value containing them causes a parse error and the entire base fails to load.

instructions.content: NEVER put status- or state-specific conditions in the top-level global filters block when different views need to show different subsets; a global filter silently excludes those notes from every view, including ones that should show them.
instructions.original_snippets: NEVER place status- or state-specific conditions in the top-level filters block when your base contains views that need to show different subsets ... Move status-specific conditions to view-level filters.

instructions.content: Use single quotes for formula strings that themselves contain double quotes, and double quotes for simple strings.
instructions.original_snippets: Use single quotes for formulas containing double quotes ... Use double quotes for simple strings

instructions.content: View types are table, cards, list, or map; a map view additionally requires latitude/longitude properties and the Maps community plugin.
instructions.original_snippets: type: table | cards | list | map ... Requires latitude/longitude properties and the Maps community plugin.

instructions.content: When validating a base, check that all referenced properties and formulas exist and that quoting/indentation matches YAML syntax rules.
instructions.original_snippets: Validate: Verify the file is valid YAML with no syntax errors. Check that all referenced properties and formulas exist. Common issues: unquoted strings containing special YAML characters, mismatched quotes in formula expressions, referencing formula.X without defining X in formulas

instructions.content: A summaries entry maps a property or formula column to an aggregation function (Average, Sum, Min, Max, etc.) shown in the view footer.
instructions.original_snippets: Define custom summary formulas ... Map properties to summary formulas
